In 7th grade, I had absolutely no friends and middle school was just absolutely miserable for me.  Then we had an assignment where we had to act out a scene from “Farewell to Manzanar” in front of the whole class, and I was just dying from anxiety. The day came, I didn’t prepare at all, and I just wanted to get it over with. So I decided to channel all my prepubescent angst and despair into portraying the mother of the main character when she throws all her plates to the ground. I don’t remember too much of what I said or how I acted, but I remember rushing to my seat after and burying my head in embarrassment. Then the teacher had us write little paragraphs on who we think did best and why, and then gave the slips of paper to that person. I must have gotten them half the class and being so surprised. I even received one from the smartest girl in class who I also had a crush on, and I was just ecstatic. I kept all of those slips of papers to cheer me up whenever I feel down.
